To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The discharge of medullary raphe magnus serotonergic cells correlates with very slow and respiratory frequency rhythms in blood pressure recordings.
the discharge of serotonergic cells of the raphe magnus region is influenced by multiple factors that include behavioral state, cold challenge, and ongoing homeostatic processes.
serotonergic RM neurons integrate information about multiple physiological activities and challenges to modulate spinal processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of brain stem serotonergic cells as modulatory neurons.
the role of the serotonergic system in the control of spinal functions and the mechanisms by which serotonergic cells receive and respond to information about homeostatic needs.
the neural basis for the regulation of homeostatic functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
serotonergic RM neurons are not a single population but a collection of neurons with different functions.
RM serotonergic cells are influenced by a number of endogenous factors, some of which are unknown.

serotonergic RM neurons integrate afferent input related to multiple homeostatic functions and challenges and can modulate spinal processes accordingly, and that this integration occurs at a level that is not dependent on baroreception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
serotonergic cells integrate information about the state of the organism and its environment and can modulate spinal and brainstem processes accordingly.

the discharge of serotonergic cells is influenced by a wide range of endogenous and exogenous stimuli and that this discharge reflects a composite of the ongoing activities and challenges of the organism.
the discharge of serotonergic cells is a function of the ongoing activities of the body.
The main takeaway from our work is that

serotonergic cell activity is not simply a function of behavioral state or of a single homeostatic challenge, but rather reflects the integration of information about multiple homeo- static challenges.

serotonergic cell activity is a by-product of the organism's ongoing homeostatic challenges and that it is not the activity of the cells that is the important variable, rather it is the modulation of the activity of the cell that is important to spinal function.
serotonergic cell activity is influenced by a variety of endogenous processes and that these influences are likely to vary with time of day and the behavioral state of the animal.
